summary:
We developed **OPPY: Mission Mars**, an educational browser game inspired by NASA’s Opportunity rover. Players drive across a simulated Martian landscape, investigate rocks, photograph the terrain and send discoveries back to Earth. Along the way, they manage solar energy, navigate obstacles and answer short science questions.

The project addresses the challenge of making space exploration understandable and engaging for young learners. It turns scientific information into decisions and discoveries, allowing students to learn through play. A discovery journal, helpful feedback and opportunities to retry support learners who need extra guidance.

The project is important because it connects space science with curiosity, problem-solving and resource management. It introduces Opportunity’s scientific legacy while clearly distinguishing verified mission facts from fictional gameplay.
details:
OPPY: Mission Mars places players in control of a virtual Opportunity rover during a fictional training expedition. Players use arrow keys, on-screen direction buttons or tap-to-drive navigation to explore a map inspired by the Martian surface.

The expedition includes three investigations: examining rocky layers for clues about ancient water, identifying a meteorite and learning how rover photographs support exploration. At each discovery site, players read a short explanation and answer a question. Correct answers unlock journal entries, while incorrect answers receive encouraging feedback and another attempt. After completing all three investigations, players return to an uplink tile to send their findings to Earth and earn a Mars Explorer badge.

An energy system adds decision-making to the adventure. Driving and investigating consume energy, while recharging restores it. Sunny tiles provide larger boosts, and simulated dust storms reduce solar charging. These simplified mechanics introduce the relationship between sunlight, rover power and exploration.

The game was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with the Canvas API drawing the terrain, rover and animated weather. Browser localStorage saves progress on the same browser. ChatGPT supported development, and NASA’s Opportunity mission information informed the educational content. No specialised hardware is required beyond a device with a modern web browser.

The creative approach combines rover navigation, resource management and science questions within one short adventure. Design considerations included simple English, readable instructions, keyboard and touch controls, untimed gameplay, retry opportunities and clear distinctions between historical facts and invented game mechanics.

The intended impact is to strengthen interest in space science and encourage observation, planning and persistence. These are intended learning benefits; classroom outcomes have not yet been measured.
